reason: Full-text proof plan: Set t=ζ_8+ζ_8^{-1}; t²=2. For q modulo 8 equal to 1 or 7, ζ_8^q+ζ_8^{-q}=t; for 3 or 5 it is −t. Thus Frob_q acts by the sign (−1)^{(q²−1)/8}. Since t²=2 and q is odd, reduction plus Euler’s criterion identifies this sign with (2/q); t remains nonzero modulo q. This is independent of the earlier second-supplement theorem. Sources inspected: Jerry Shurman, Math 361 Ninth Lecture, §§2–3; J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Ch. 6 and Ch. 8 Examples 8.18–8.19.
